newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo gold futures rise on weak yen.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo gold futures rise on weak yen.

text.p: Yen-denominated gold futures extended gains late in Monday trade to end mostly at the day's highs as the dollar rose further against the yen, traders said.
Gold futures ranged from unchanged to nine yen per gram higher. Benchmark August was nine yen up at 1,346 yen.
Spot gold prices reacted little to Iraq's military moves against Kurdish minorities in the north of the country at the weekend, they said.
Spot gold was quoted at $386.70/387.00 per ounce at the Tokyo close, against $386.50/387.00 in New York on Friday.

"The rising tensions in Iraq are likely to provide psychological support to gold prices, but will not be enough to push up prices significantly at the moment," a trading house trader said. He pegged initial resistance for gold at $389.00 per ounce.

In the gold futures market, the benchmark August contract remained confined within its prolonged range of between 1,330 and 1,350 yen per gram. Traders said participation by private investors was still limited, adding that the market was unlikely to attract much business from private investors unless it breaks out of its current ranges.
